It consists of galvanized hardware cloth and nonwoven geotextile being secured over the steel grates of the catch basins, with 6 inches of stone being placed over that to allow stormwater to flow through while filtering out sediment. Once construction is complete AGIP is removed from all catch basins. These controls are temporary and will be removed as construction concludes. A Stabilized Construction Entrance at the site’s main road entrance at Pendola Point Road will be used as additional temporary protection while construction occurs on site. This prevents the entrance to the site from deteriorating into an unsafe and inaccessible area due to consistent heavy loads passing over unstable ground. This will be removed once construction of the road is nearing completion. A retention pond will be created to which all draining infrastructure on the site leads. Such a retention pond is required by Hillsborough County and SWFWMD (Southwest Florida Water Management District) to manage stormwater runoff and improve water quality by capturing and treating pollutants. These systems help prevent flooding by storing water, allowing sediment to settle out, and providing filtration before water eventually discharges into natural water bodies. Once the main site civil works are completed the focus will shift to the plant, equipment and module foundations. 4.10.3 CONSTRUCTION BERTH PREPARATION This new berth to be used only for equipment delivery during hub construction could be made ready at the same time as, or possibly even earlier than, the site civil works. It would then be available to be used for the material, equipment, and fabrication arrivals, allowing them to be transferred directly onto the site. With all materials being laid out at the storage / laydown areas, construction can commence and then follow a planned sequence of procurement deliveries and onto installation builds. This negates the requirement of allocating the ‘future’ northeast site areas as a materials warehousing area. Marine Off-Loading by Crane Lifts With civil ground works completed two heavy-lift (700tn) crawler cranes can be brought in by barge and offloaded. The cranes will be positioned on the site-edge area north of the LPG pipeline, one to the east with the other to the west and made ready for material arrivals on cargo barges which will berth alongside Page95 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version the pontoon. A third may be added further west to enable direct crane lifts over to the actual worksites without having to relocate one of the offloading cranes. Marine Off-Loading to Site Transfers (Option 1) The fabrications / equipment packages will be offloaded to the storage areas by SMPT’s or lifted from the vessels directly by the cranes into the prepared embankment laydown areas to be stored while awaiting a scheduled transfer across the pipeline and onto the site.
